name: net-a2-simulation-clock
title: Netcode A2: SimulationClock, 64-bit tick counter (Time::GetTick), timeScale-independent fixed dt and tick-boundary attach queue in the network presets; the None preset is byte-for-byte unchanged
issue: USER DECISIONS (2026-10-20, all final, do NOT revisit): cross-platform determinism is the target; THREE built-in presets: None (offline default), Server authoritative (PhysX + prediction + reconciliation), Deterministic lockstep/rollback (cross-platform; needs a deterministic backend from #156 which does not exist yet); D3 the Deterministic preset is shown DISABLED with the reason while no backend declares CrossPlatform; D4 the engine REFUSES to start a Deterministic project whose requirements are unmet; netcode decisions N1-N15 of C:/Method Notes Obsidian/orchestrator/proposals/netcode-runtime-design.md are accepted as recommended (own UDP layer, WebSocket first, star topology via N2Server relay, lockstep before rollback, opt-in field replication, new N2Server executable, v1 prediction limited to owned kinematic/character movement, etc.). Read C:/Method Notes Obsidian/orchestrator/proposals/netcode-runtime-design.md (sections 2.4, 5, 7.2 and the 'Decisions for the user' list) and C:/Method Notes Obsidian/orchestrator/proposals/physx-limitations-and-determinism.md (4.1-4.4 and 5) FULLY first, plus docs/physics.html and the determinism docs pages (find them: grep docs/ for determinism, luaSeed, simdTier, strict). THIS ITEM IS PR A2 (tick ownership); A1 (settings/presets) is a parallel item that touches Application::Init and health code: keep your Application.cpp changes confined to the tick/run path and rebase carefully; if you need the preset value, read it through a small accessor that works whether or not A1 has merged (default none) and note it. SCOPE per C:/Method Notes Obsidian/orchestrator/proposals/netcode-runtime-design.md 2.4 and C:/Method Notes Obsidian/orchestrator/proposals/physx-limitations-and-determinism.md B5: today Application::Tick adds the real frame delta (clamped at 0.25 s, dropping the rest) to an accumulator and runs PhysicsUpdate while it holds a step; the step is fixedUnscaled * timeScale; ProcessAttachQueue runs once per frame before the fixed steps; Update uses a variable dt; there is no tick counter (verify all of this in engine/src/Application.cpp, Time.cpp, Application.hpp; TickOptions::deltaSeconds already lets a host step time exactly). Build: (1) a `SimulationClock` (engine/include/engine/... pick the right place) that decides how many fixed ticks run this frame and owns a 64-bit tick counter exposed as `Time::GetTick()` (0 before the first tick, increments once per fixed tick, never wraps in practice); in the NONE preset (and whenever no network preset is configured) the existing loop runs EXACTLY as today: add a golden/characterisation test that a stepped sequence of frame deltas (incl. >0.25 s spikes, timeScale 0, 0.5, 2) gives identical tick/step counts, accumulator state and physics dt to the pre-change code (derive the expected numbers from the CURRENT code paths before changing them and keep them as test constants). (2) in a network preset (authoritative or deterministic; select by the preset setting: if A1 is not merged yet, expose a SetSimulationMode/option on Application that a test can set and that A1/netcode will drive later): Time::GetFixedDeltaTime() is independent of timeScale (timeScale becomes presentation-only for Update, or is refused/logged: choose per the proposal and record as a deviation), ProcessAttachQueue runs at each TICK BOUNDARY (before that tick's fixed step) so a component created during a tick joins the simulation at a deterministic tick, no time is dropped silently (a clock too far behind reports it via a callback/state flag for the netcode to resync, instead of clamping), FixedUpdate runs per tick with the fixed dt; Update keeps a variable dt for presentation. A stepping API for tests/headless hosts: run exactly N ticks. (3) Lua and C++ bindings: expose Time.tick (read-only) to Lua next to the existing Time bindings; document. (4) TESTS (all legs incl. web where the engine tests run): the characterisation test for None; tick counter monotonic and exactly one increment per fixed tick; network mode ignores timeScale for the step; attach queue boundary: an object spawned in a tick gets its physics body at the next tick boundary on every run, independent of frame timing (run the same scenario with different frame delta partitions and assert identical tick-by-tick results); no silent drop: a huge delta runs the ticks it owes (bounded by an explicit max-catch-up setting that reports), headless stepping API. (5) DOCS: docs on the time/application loop (find: grep docs/ for Time.fixedDeltaTime, timeScale, FixedUpdate) describing the clock, the tick counter, the network-mode differences and the None guarantee; docs/testing.html; verify against code. Nothing builds locally; CI is the test; expect fix rounds. Unverified: real network behaviour (later PRs).
acceptance: SimulationClock and Time::GetTick exist; None preset behaviour proven unchanged by a characterisation test
Network mode: timeScale-independent fixed dt, tick-boundary attach queue, no silent time drop, headless N-tick stepping
Lua Time.tick exposed; tests across frame partitions give identical tick results
All 10 checks green; docs verified against code
notes: Reviewer: the None path is untouched (diff the loop), characterisation constants really derive from the old code, tick counter semantics, attach-queue boundary correct for spawns made in Update/FixedUpdate/Lua coroutines, no silent drop, no behaviour change for the editor host/play paths (Application::Tick callers), docs true, mediums count.
